openings.claim: Freezing hold locations throughout the evening could prevent stale addresses: retain new arrivals on the existing cart and defer moves until the window ends.
openings.delta: Change when books move, rather than improving surname dividers or refreshing exception records. Keep reader records behind the desk and the clerk as sole handoff operator.
openings.prediction: For books with verified opening locations, second-location searches decline without surname corrections; cart pickups remain fast within its observed capacity.
openings.rival_prediction: Correcting household surnames is the nearest alternative: delays decline principally for corrected mismatches, while location freezing alone leaves those delays.
openings.defeat: Verified unchanged locations still produce comparable second searches, cart congestion slows retrieval, or preparation exceeds ten minutes.
openings.probe: The clerk trials a batch already fitting the cart, records initial locations privately, leaves it stationary during the window, and uses the existing timing sheet for searches, handoff accuracy and preparation time. This evaluates a bounded probe; whole-window efficacy remains unproven.
assumptions: The cart can accommodate evening arrivals without blocking access.
All daily preparation stays within ten clerk-minutes.

openings.claim: Assign stable numbered shelf sectors and keep a private paper reader-to-sector index, making physical retrieval independent of household surname ordering.
openings.delta: Replace surname as the storage address; existing divider cards mark sectors and paper maps reader associations to them.
openings.prediction: Household-name mismatches cease to require another physical search when the association and sector entry are correct.
openings.rival_prediction: Repairing surname placement predicts similar gains without index upkeep; numbered sectors should additionally tolerate a changed household surname association without moving the book.
openings.defeat: Index lookup or upkeep erases retrieval gains, entries become stale, wrong-reader handoffs occur, or preparation exceeds ten minutes.
openings.probe: Trial one existing shelf section within the preparation cap; record retrieval times and privately verify reader-book associations. Compare mismatch cases with surname correction. The bounded trial does not establish the 95% target.
assumptions: Index creation and maintenance fit the preparation cap at full volume.
Reader-book association can be verified privately.
Numbered sectors remain legible and books fit existing shelves.
